How to configure for port 443 ? Would the current implementation allow ? The meson option `additional-support-bootstrap-credetial` would allow for current operating port to work normally as well ?

With the current design of BMCWeb, you can't not configure port 443. because it is duplicated with main BMCWeb socket which are listening on all of BMC network interfaces.
We need drive the redfish host interface request to different BMCWeb socket which support BootStrap credentials.
Supported use port 443.
this should be 443, right?

The current BMCWeb server listening on the HTTPS Ports 443  of all BMC internet interfaces (eth0, eth1, usb0). So all of request will come to that server instance (I call it is main BMCWeb server).
The key point of this design spec is using on different BMCWeb server instance for Redfish host interface (I call RHI BMCWeb server). That instance will be bound to one specific ethernet device in this case is usb0.
Because main BMCWeb server is listing on port 443 of usb0 so the RHI BMCWeb server have to listen on different port.

The latest patches create a bootstrap0 user like you suggest here and then reverts back to making users with random names...

I'm not sure what this means exactly.  You'd want to leave the user enabled, otherwise it wouldn't' work for login, right?

> if the command is run multiple times, what should the behavior be?

I'd assume the credentials match the last password requested?  Ideally there's something tied to boot state, but I'm not an expert on whether IPMI knows the host boot status.

> The latest patches create a bootstrap0 user like you suggest here and then reverts back to making users with random names...

Randomly named users seems unfriendly to humans that ever have to debug this.  "bootstrap" (or some other well chosen name) at least gives the user a hint why there's two users in their system now.

> You'd want to leave the user enabled

The thing being left enabled by the modifier is credential bootstrapping, not the user.

> I'd assume the credentials match the last password requested?
No, the spec says this:

If the get bootstrap account credentials command is sent subsequent times and responds with the completion code 00h, a new account shall be created based on the newly generated credentials. Any existing bootstrap accounts shall remain active.

> Randomly named users seems unfriendly to humans

Agree but the original question remains...what to name the subsequently created bootstrap users?  bootstrap0..N ?

> Any existing bootstrap accounts shall remain active.

Is there a reason it was implemented this way?  Why do we enable more than one bootstrap user at a time?

The bootStrap account can be used in different applications or system services, limit one bootStrap account will require sharing the bootStrap account in EDK.

This is "Introduction" about Redfish host interface in DSP0270 V1.3.3.
```
In many management schemes, it is necessary to provide
standardized Redfish-based communication between the host CPU and the Redfish service in the
management unit. This communication is in addition to the Redfish services available via the external
network. Implementation of the Redfish host interface is optional for the system designer. If provided,
this interface may be used in both the pre-boot (firmware) stage and by drivers and applications within
the host operating system and is designed to be available without use of external networking.
```

Just so we're clear, this is doing a blocking IO read of a SPI based interface in the middle of an io reactor.  This is really pointing to the central problem here that the filesystem is not an IPC, so we don't have the proper primitives for dealing with it in an async fashion.

If we wanted to, we have uring support now, and it would be easy to turn on, but lets just not use the filesystem as ipc.
